claims.text: A Moment Tensor Potential trained by active learning on DFT data can be combined with CPA-derived properties for Ta-containing refractory multi-principal-element alloys.
The MTP training data should include surfaces and unstable stacking-fault configurations.
CPA can provide elastic constants and misfit volumes for the proposed hybrid framework.
CPA-derived elastic constants and misfit volumes ensure global thermodynamic consistency of a melting free-energy model.
The target material is a disordered, Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy such as MoNbTaW.
Standard experimental melting measurements are infeasible for the target alloy.
DFT-based thermodynamic integration is computationally prohibitive for the target alloy.
Replacing full thermodynamic integration with an MTP-based perturbation calculation will retain melting free-energy accuracy while reducing computational cost.
The proposed calculations apply near melting at temperatures above 1500 K.
Severe local lattice distortion is characteristic of refractory high-entropy alloys and must be represented in the training configurations.
Local lattice distortion and short-range order govern the solid-liquid free-energy landscape.
CPA efficiently models global elastic properties while MTP accurately models local atomic relaxation around surfaces and defects.
Training on high-energy defect configurations rather than liquid configurations is sufficient to capture the subtle free-energy differences needed for melting predictions.
The free-energy surface is sufficiently smooth near the solid-liquid transition for a reduced perturbation scheme when local distortions are modeled correctly.
The proposed method will achieve less than 1 meV/atom error relative to high-fidelity melting free-energy benchmarks.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than a factor of four relative to DFT thermodynamic integration.
Empirical EAM potentials fail to capture complex liquid structure and lattice distortion in multicomponent systems.
The hypothesis is limited to BCC refractory HEAs in which local lattice distortion dominates strengthening and stability.
Fermi-surface transitions, omitted magnetic effects, or liquid short-range order absent from the training set can cause the method to fail.
A defect- and surface-focused training set may inadequately sample the liquid configurations required for accurate melting thermodynamics.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome applies a less-than-1 meV/atom error margin to both melting temperature and free-energy difference, while the falsification rule describes a melting-temperature error as greater than 1 meV/atom or greater than 100 K. Temperature error cannot be expressed in meV/atom without an explicit thermodynamic conversion.

The mechanism asserts that defect-focused training is sufficient to predict liquid melting thermodynamics, whereas the uncertainty field explicitly states that this training set may not adequately sample the liquid. This is framed as uncertainty, but it directly weakens the asserted mechanism.
